                                  ORDER GRANTING VARIANCE

        THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE”) Notice Under Rule 17.9.530.11(A)

and Verified Petition for Variance (“Petition”). The Commission grants EPE’s variance request,

as it meets the requirements of Rules 17.9.530.11(A) and 1.2.2.40 NMAC, achieves the purpose

of Rules 17.9.530.13(Q)(6) and 17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC, and is in the public interest.

                                        BACKGROUND

        1.       On December 4, 2025, EPE filed its Petition requesting a variance of Schedule Q-

6 under Rules 17.9.530.13(Q)(6) and 17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC for EPE’s forthcoming Minimum

Data Requirements Filing Package in support of its February 2026 application for revision of retail

rates. Specifically, EPE requests a variance to file its audit report prepared under 18 C.F.R. Part

41 for calendar year 2024 when it becomes available around mid-April 2026. 1

        2.       On December 8, 2025, the Commission issued its Order Setting Deadlines for

Responses and Replies, which set December 12, 2025, as the deadline for responses.

        3.       No responses were filed.

                                            DISCUSSION

        4.       The Commission grants EPE’s variance request because it complies with Rules

17.9.530.11(A) and 1.2.2.40 NMAC, achieves the purpose of Rules 17.9.530.13(Q)(6) and

17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC, and is in the public interest.



1 Petition (December 4, 2025) at 1.
          5.       Under Rule 17.9.530.11(A) NMAC, “an applicant utility unable to comply fully

with any data request contained in Appendix A [of Rule 17.9.530 NMAC] due to good and

sufficient cause should give notice in writing to the Commission of the applicant utility’s inability

to comply with the provisions of such data request at least thirty (30) days prior to the actual filing

of the Minimum Data Requirements Filing Package.”

         6.       Rules 1.2.2.40(E)(1)-(5) NMAC provide that a request for a variance from a

requirement of any Commission rule shall: (a) identify the section of the rule from which the

variance is requested; (b) describe the situation that necessitates the variance; (c) describe the effect

of complying with the rule on the applicant if the variance is not granted; (d) describe the result

the variance will have if granted; and (e) describe how the proposed alternative will achieve the

purpose of the rule, and why it is in the public interest.

         7.       Rule 1.2.2.40(B) NMAC requires a petition for variance to be supported by an

affidavit signed by an officer of the applicant with authority to sign for the applicant.

         8.       EPE anticipates filing a rate case application in February 2026. 2 Under

Commission rules, that filing must include certain minimum data requirements. 3

         9.       EPE filed its Petition on December 4, 2025, which is more than thirty days prior to

February 1, 2026.

         10.      EPE responds to each of the requirements in Rules 1.2.2.40(E)(1)-(5) NMAC as

follows:

                  a. EPE seeks a variance from Rule 17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC, which requires the
                     utility to “submit a copy of the opinion of its independent certified public
                     accountant stating that an independent examination of the book amounts and
                     accounting adjustments thereto of the applicant utility company's books and
                     records has been made for the Base Period, as defined herein, and that the results

2 Petition ¶ 8.
3 Rule 17.9.530.6 NMAC.

                           thereof are in all material respects in compliance with the Uniform System of
                          Accounts prescribed by the New Mexico Public Service Commission [New
                          Mexico Public Regulation Commission].”

                   b. EPE must comply with the audit requirements of 18 C.F.R. Part 41, which
                      utilizes the “Uniform System of Accounts” defined in Rule 17.3.510.10 NMAC,
                      and therefore if EPE’s audit period were the same for 18 C.F.R. Part 41 and its
                      Base Period, then the annual audit under 18 C.F.R. Part 41 would satisfy the
                      requirements of Rule 530.14(Q)(6). 4 However, EPE’s audit reports under 18
                      C.F.R. Part 41 examine EPE’s records for a calendar year, the most recent report
                      available is for calendar year 2024, and therefore the 2024 report covers the first
                      three months of EPE’s anticipated Base Period for the rate case it will be filing,
                      but does not cover the entire Base Period. 5 EPE anticipates that the audit of the
                      remaining portion of the Base Period will be available for filing in mid-April
                      2026. 6 Since EPE has chosen a Base Period of October 1, 2024 through
                      September 30, 2025, and the Base Period may not be more than one hundred
                      fifty days prior to the date of tender for filing, it follows that EPE must file its
                      application within 150 days of September 30, 2025, and the 2025 audit report
                      will not be completed in time for that filing. 7

                   c. Preparing a separate audit of EPE’s books and records to comply with Rule 530
                      Schedule Q-6 for the Base Period would entail a substantial expense that EPE
                      estimates would be no less than $250,000 and may be as much as $600,000, and
                      would duplicate the work EPE must undertake to comply with 18 C.F.R. Part
                      41. 8 EPE further asserts that preparing a separate audit would be inconsistent
                      with the language in Rule 530.14(Q) requiring an applicant to submit the most
                      current reports available. 9

                   d. If a variance is granted, EPE will file its 2025 annual audit containing the
                      remaining nine months of the Base Period (January through September 2025)
                      within five (5) business days of the date it files with FERC pursuant to 18 C.F.R.
                      Part 41, EPE will not incur the costs associated with a separate audit to comply
                      with Rule 530 Schedule Q-6, and the Commission will receive the required
                      information “within months of EPE’s application under NMPRC Rule 17.1.2.10
                      and before any hearing on the case is likely to occur.” 10

                   e. EPE identifies that the purpose of Rule 530 is to define the minimum data
                      requirements necessary to evaluate an application under Rule 17.1.1.20 NMAC,
                      and asserts that:

                           i.“[t]he requested variance is consistent with that purpose because [EPE]
                           will provide the information responsive to Schedule Q-6 that is available
                           at the time of filing and will supplement to provide the remaining
                           information well before any hearing or decision on the application,” 11
                           and
                       ii. “[t]he requested variance is consistent with the public interest because
                           it prevents [EPE] from incurring unnecessary and duplicative costs that
                           may ultimately affect the costs borne by ratepayers. EPE will perform
                           the required audits in accordance with 18 C.F.R. Part 41 and should not
                           be required to incur duplicative costs under Rule 530 merely because
                           the 2025 audit will not be available for filing until April 2026.”

          11.   Staff does not oppose EPE’s Petition, with the understanding that the audited

numbers do not change the February filing. 12

          12.   EPE’s Petition complies with each requirement of Rule 1.2.2.40(E) NMAC,

achieves the purpose of Rules 17.9.530.13(Q)(6) and 17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC by ensuring that

EPE will submit the required data “well before” the hearing in this case, and is in the public interest

because it prevents EPE incurring unnecessary and duplicative costs that could increase the costs

borne by ratepayers.

                               FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS

          13.   EPE’s requested variance should be granted because EPE’s Petition meets the

requirements of Rules 17.9.530.11(A) and 1.2.2.40 NMAC, achieves the purpose of Rules

17.9.530.13(Q)(6) and 17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC, and is in the public interest.

          14.   If the audited numbers in EPE’s supplemental filing of required data change the

numbers that EPE files in its February rate case application, then EPE shall concurrently make a

filing that details the changes to the numbers, and details the effect upon the requests that EPE will

have submitted in its rate case application.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.       EPE is granted its requested variance from Rules 17.9.530.13(Q)(6) and

17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC for its forthcoming Filing Package in support of an application for new

rate schedule under Rule 17.1.2.10 NMAC, anticipated in February 2026.

       B.       EPE shall file its 2025 annual audit containing the remaining nine months of the

Base Period within five business days of the date EPE files with FERC pursuant to 18 C.F.R. Part

41. This filing shall be made into the rate case docket.

       C.       If EPE has not filed with the Commission its 2025 annual audit containing the

remaining nine months of the Base Period by April 27, 2026, then EPE shall make a filing by April

27, 2026 that explains the unanticipated delay in the filing of the 2025 annual audit.

       D.       If the audited numbers in EPE’s supplemental filing of required data change the

numbers that EPE files in its February rate case application, then EPE shall concurrently make a

filing into the rate case docket that details the changes to the numbers, and details the effect upon

the requests that EPE will have submitted in its rate case application.

       E.       This Order is effective when signed.

       F.       The Commission shall serve a copy of this Order upon all persons listed on the

attached Certificate of Service via e-mail if their e-mail addresses are known, and otherwise, via

regular mail.

       G.       In computing time in accordance with statute, regulation, or Commission order, the

computation shall begin on the date that this Order is filed with the Chief Clerk of the

Commission’s Records Management Bureau or the Chief Clerk’s designee.
